newsitem.title: UK: Lasmo firm after Merrill recommendation.
newsitem.headline: Lasmo firm after Merrill recommendation.

text.p: Shares in Lasmo Plc were firm against a sharply lower market trend on Monday as analysts at Merrill Lynch repeated an "accumulate" rating on the oil stock, traders said.

Lasmo shares were up 1/2p at 203 by 1039 GMT in trading volume of 675,479 shares, after reaching a four-year high of 218p on September 10. The FTSE 100 by contrast was down 39.1 points or one percent at 3,925.0.
Merrill analyst James Cartwright said Lasmo had emerged from a lengthy restructuring as a lower cost company with significant growth opportunities.

He said Lasmo was among the most leveraged oil stocks to higher crude prices, with every $1 rise in the price of crude lifting 1997 earnings expectations by some 25 percent, based on an average price of $17.80 a barrel.

Cartwright said the potential of Lasmo's Algerian discoveries had been only partly reflected in its share price and pointed out the stock was trading at a discount to Merrill's base asset value estimate of 213p per share.
Merrill has a 12-month price target of 225p per share for Lasmo shares and expects the company's pre-tax profit to rise to 221.9 million stg in 1996 from 144.0 million stg in 1995.
